skill.name: add-event-type
skill.description: Guides adding a new React and TypeScript event type to a frontend feed system, including types, block rendering, and WebSocket handling.
skill.summary: Add React feed event types with matching TypeScript definitions and UI blocks.
skill.author: AppleLamps

content.value_statement: Frontend feed changes often require updates across types, blocks, rendering, and WebSocket handling. This skill guides a consistent React and TypeScript event addition.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the existing EventType union in the frontend feed file.
Guides creation of a typed interface for the new event payload.
Adds the new event type to the existing TypeScript union.
Creates a React block component that follows current UI patterns.
Points to feed rendering and WebSocket handler updates when needed.
Emphasizes complete TypeScript types without using the any type.
limitations: It assumes the feed system uses React and TypeScript.
It does not define backend event contracts beyond handler guidance.
It does not generate automated tests by itself.
It needs the repository to contain the referenced frontend feed structure.

use_cases.title: Display New Agent Output
use_cases.description: Add a feed block for a new assistant response type with a typed payload and visible UI treatment.

use_cases.title: Standardize Feed Extensions
use_cases.description: Help a team add event blocks with consistent naming, styling, and rendering patterns.

use_cases.title: Wire Backend Events To UI
use_cases.description: Extend a WebSocket-driven feed so new backend messages appear in the React interface.

prompt_templates.title: Add A Simple Event
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one visible feed block.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a new progress_update event type to the frontend feed and create a matching React block.

prompt_templates.title: Match Existing Styling
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request focused on UI consistency.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a search_result event type. Follow the existing feed block styles and keep the TypeScript payload complete.

prompt_templates.title: Connect WebSocket Messages
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with backend message handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add an error_report event type and update the WebSocket message handler if it maps backend events to feed items.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Feed Addition
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the new event type implementation for naming, union coverage, rendering coverage, and TypeScript completeness.

output_examples.input: Add a new search_result event type.
output_examples.output: The feed supports search results with a typed event payload, a matching block component, and rendering coverage in the main feed.

output_examples.input: Create a block for displaying errors.
output_examples.output: The UI now has an error event type, an error-focused feed block, and guidance for WebSocket handling if backend events provide it.

output_examples.input: Add event type for progress updates.
output_examples.output: Progress updates are represented as a typed feed event and rendered through a component that follows existing layout and styling conventions.

best_practices: Review existing event blocks before adding a new component.
Keep event names in snake case and component names in PascalCase.
Test the new event with a mock WebSocket message or fixture.
anti_patterns: Do not add a feed block without updating the EventType union.
Do not use loose any types for new event payload fields.
Do not introduce styling that conflicts with existing Tailwind patterns.

faq.question: What framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets a React frontend that uses TypeScript event types for a feed system.

faq.question: Does it update backend code?
faq.answer: It only reminds the agent to update WebSocket handling when backend messages require it.

faq.question: Can it add multiple event types?
faq.answer: Yes, but each event should still receive its own typed payload and rendering path.

faq.question: Does it require Claude or Codex?
faq.answer: The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What files does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects a frontend feed file like frontend/src/App.tsx with event types and block components.

faq.question: How should output be tested?
faq.answer: Send or mock the new event through the feed path and confirm the block renders correctly.
